instruction: Switch on the screen reader for audio reading of text.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: SCREEN_READER=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-reader-enabled 2>/dev/null | grep -c true); if [ "$SCREEN_READER" -gt 0 ]; then echo "Screen reader enabled"; else echo "Screen reader disabled"; fi

metadata.explanation: This task requires enabling the screen reader (Orca). The evaluator checks if org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-reader-enabled is set to true. This is similar in difficulty to the original task - both require navigating accessibility settings and enabling a single feature. No custom functions needed as we use existing check_include_exclude metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses vm_command_line getter to check the GNOME gsettings key 'org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-reader-enabled'
Command logic is correct: uses gsettings to read screen reader state, grep to count 'true' occurrences, and outputs appropriate message
Metric function check_include_exclude correctly receives rules dict as parameter (framework calls get_rule which returns config['rules'] directly)
Expected values are semantically correct: 'Screen reader enabled' for success case, excludes 'Screen reader disabled' and 'error' for failure cases
Complete coverage: The single requirement (turn on screen reader) is fully verified by checking the gsettings state
Logic will work correctly at runtime: gsettings is the standard way to verify screen reader state in GNOME/Ubuntu
